description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

With over half a billion rides and counting, Lyft is solving hard problems in a flourishing domain with a lot of data and creative solutions in Marketplace, Mapping, Fraud, Growth and beyond. We're actively building the next-generation Machine Learning (ML) platform for low-cost, ultra-immersive transportation to improve people’s lives using modern ML with petabyte-scale data. Our Machine Learning Engineers are excited to work on these challenging problems and redefine solutions to directly impact various aspects of Lyft's primary business.

As a PhD Machine Learning Engineer Intern on our Applied AI team, you'll take on an open research problem tied to product experiences used by millions of riders. Working closely with a Staff ML Engineer mentor, you'll scope the problem, develop and evaluate new methods on real data, and take the work far enough that it can be shared with the research community, with the goal of a paper submission to a top ML venue.

If you are a PhD student who enjoys turning open-ended research questions into working systems, and you want your research to be tested against real users and real data, this opportunity is for you!

Responsibilities:

  • Own a research project from start to finish: frame the problem, review related work, propose new methods, and design rigorous offline and online evaluations
  • Design, build, train and test ML models in areas such as reinforcement learning, sequential decision-making, personalization
  • Write production-quality code that turns research prototypes into working pipelines on Lyft's data and ML infrastructure
  • Partner with Product Managers, Data Scientists, and fellow ML Engineers to frame research questions within the business context
  • Analyze experimental and observational data, and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Write up results for publication at a peer-reviewed venue, with support from your mentor and the team
  • Participate in code and spec reviews to ensure code quality and distribute knowledge

Experience:

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field, and returning to your program after the internship, with a graduation date between December 2027 and Summer 2028 (required)
  • A track record of ML research, shown through publications, preprints, or substantial research projects
  • Strong foundation in reinforcement learning and sequential decision making, especially problems with delayed or long-horizon rewards
  • Solid grounding in both causal inference and counterfactual evaluation
  • Good understanding of ML libraries like PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX
  • Strong programming skills in Python or a similar language
  • Proven ability to effectively turn research ML papers into working code
  • Curiosity and ability to quickly learn new concepts and technologies
  • Strong problem solving mindset, resourcefulness, and willingness to figure things out independently through research or collaboratively through brainstorming

    • Practical knowledge of how to build efficient end-to-end ML workflows on large-scale data (for example Spark or SQL)
    • Familiarity with online experimentation and A/B testing

description:
About Marshall Wace

Marshall Wace is a leading global alternatives investment manager with around $85bn in assets under management and over 700 employees working across London, New York, Hong Kong, Singapore, Shanghai, and Abu Dhabi.  Operating as a single team across the globe, we are dedicated to creating long-term relationships with our clients built on trust and integrity. We define our culture as one of continuous innovation and a quest for improvement. We instinctively strive to do things differently, with fresh thinking that enables us to create proprietary value and maximise the benefits to our clients.

We manage quantitative, systematic, and fundamental strategies, specializing predominantly in long/short equity. Our strategies are implemented globally, leveraging proprietary systems and processes. Technology and data have been at the core of our business for more than two decades. In 2002, we launched MW TOPS, the world’s first ‘Alpha Capture’ application. Today, we continue to foster an environment focused on innovation and the pursuit of excellence.

The Opportunity

The Quant Implementation team builds the systems that connect quantitative research to live trading within Marshall Wace’s systematic investment business. Quantitative developers design, implement and maintain alpha algorithms and portfolio construction processes, translating research ideas into robust production systems. The role combines quantitative problem-solving with software engineering and the challenge of operating reliable, high-performance systems at scale.

As a Quant Implementation Intern, you will gain first-hand exposure to the full lifecycle of a systematic investment idea—from research and data analysis through portfolio construction, implementation and performance monitoring. This is not a pure software engineering internship: you will use technology as a tool to solve investment problems and will develop an understanding of how systematic strategies make decisions, manage risk and generate trades.

You will join a collaborative global team and contribute to meaningful projects with direct relevance to the investment process. The internship is well suited to someone who enjoys combining quantitative thinking, markets and hands-on problem solving.

What You Will Do

  • Analyse market and portfolio data to understand signal behaviour, trading outcomes and strategy performance.
  • Help validate new models and portfolio construction changes before they are introduced into live trading.
  • Investigate differences between research expectations and real-world results, considering data, market, risk and implementation effects.
  • Contribute clean, reliable code to systems that support live systematic strategies.

Examples of Internship Projects

  • Analysing how transaction costs, liquidity or portfolio constraints affect a strategy’s realised performance.
  • Building analytics to explain portfolio positioning, risk exposures or recent trading activity.
  • Improving a portfolio construction process to support a new market, instrument or investment objective.
  • Developing monitoring that helps the team identify unusual model or trading behaviour.

What We Are Looking For

  • Currently studying toward a master’s or PhD in a quantitative subject such as computer science, mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering or a related discipline.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an interest in applying them to financial markets.
  • Programming experience in Python, MATLAB, C++, Java or a similar language.
  • A solid foundation in probability, statistics, linear algebra or numerical methods.
  • Curiosity about systematic investing and a desire to understand why a strategy works—not only how to code it.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively across research and technology teams.
  • Care, ownership and sound judgement when working with data and code.

Prior finance experience is helpful but not required. We are more interested in evidence of intellectual curiosity, rigorous thinking and enthusiasm for learning how quantitative ideas are translated into live investment decisions.

What You Will Gain

  • Direct exposure to systematic investing and the practical decisions behind live portfolios and trades.
  • Experience working alongside quantitative researchers, traders and experienced developers.
  • An understanding of the gap between a promising research result and a robust, scalable investment process.
  • Mentoring, technical guidance and opportunities to learn about different strategies, markets and asset classes.
  • The opportunity to see your work contribute to real investment workflows during the internship.

Why Join Us?

This internship offers a rare combination of quantitative research, software engineering and commercial investment exposure. You will work on problems where technical quality matters because the output influences real portfolios, while developing a practical understanding of markets and systematic trading.

We value people who ask thoughtful questions, challenge assumptions and work collaboratively to deliver results. If you are excited by the idea of using quantitative methods and technology to help turn investment research into live trading, we would like to hear from you.

You will apply foundational biological and laboratory principles in a fast-paced environment and are expected to:

  • Help maintain, calibrate, and operate advanced optical hardware, lightsheet imaging systems, and automated histology equipment
  • Support routine tissue processing, embedding, sectioning (microtomy), slide preparation, and standard/special staining protocols
  • Document experimental protocols, image acquisition parameters, and data analysis pipelines in compliance with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and laboratory SOPs

  • 6+ months of relevant academic coursework or wet-lab experience handling biological tissues and standard histology techniques (e.g., tissue fixation, sectioning, or fluorescence imaging)

  • Experience with 3D image analysis software or large volume rendering tools (e.g., Imaris, ImageJ/Fiji, or Python/MATLAB image processing libraries)

  • Proven ability to learn new laboratory equipment quickly and troubleshoot technical procedures

Now, here's what we're building, and where you come in.

About the Role

Value Engineering at Relay is the bridge between frontline operational reality and enterprise investment decisions. Our Value Engineers parachute into a prospect's world, learn how they operate, and build the financial case that proves Relay's ROI at the C-suite level. This is analytical, customer-facing, high-stakes work. This internship puts you in the middle of it.

The Value Engineering Internship is a two-phase opportunity: a Spring semester engagement (January start, part-time) that potentially feeds into a full-time 40-hour/week Summer internship for top performers. Both phases are on-site at Relay's world-class Raleigh HQ, located near the Lenovo Center.

Strong performance creates a pathway to a return offer for a Summer or Fall 2027 internship and full-time consideration upon graduation, based on business needs.

You'll work directly with our Manager, Value Engineering, and the broader GTM org. This includes Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, and senior leadership — on live enterprise deals.

About the Team

The Value Engineering team exists to close two critical gaps: leadership isn't always in touch with the factory floor, and new technology doesn't always translate into operational impact. We bridge both by quantifying Relay's value proposition, building investment-grade business cases, and acting as a forcing function for customer ROI. Our work shapes the enterprise sales motion, customer relationships, product roadmap, and company strategy.

Responsibilities

  • Support the development of executive-level business cases that translate frontline operational data into P&L-level ROI.
  • Map prospect workflows and analyze operational metrics to identify Relay's highest-impact use cases.

  • No employer work authorization sponsorship available — candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship, now or in the future.

  • Coursework or project experience in operations research, systems engineering, supply chain, or financial analysis.

By mid-summer, you're running financial models and contributing to business cases with real ownership — not just support. By the final showcase, you've presented work that a senior leader would put in front of a Fortune 500 prospect.

About Us

Salient Motion is building a modular motion and actuation platform that is redefining how aerospace, defense, and industrial systems are designed, built, and deployed. We move fast, operate with high ownership, and expect real contribution from every member of the team. Co-ops are treated like engineers, not observers. You will own real work, ship to production hardware, and leave with a body of work you can point to.

Role Overview

As an Engineering Co-op, you will embed with our engineering team across mechanical, electrical, software, manufacturing, and systems-level work for six months or longer. Unlike a short summer internship, this role is designed for students who want to take a project from specification through qualification, see a full product cycle, and operate as a contributing member of the team.

This is a hands-on role in a fast-paced startup environment. You will be expected to ramp quickly, take ownership of a defined workstream, and ship work that goes into customer programs.

What You Will Do

  • Own a scoped engineering workstream from design through test and release, with support from a senior engineer
  • Design, build, and test electro-mechanical systems and subassemblies on active customer programs
  • Build, maintain and improve test fixtures, data collection infrastructures
  • Firmware bring-up, design validation tests for electronics boards
  • Lead prototyping, assembly, and hands-on lab and shop work
  • Plan and execute engineering tests, collect data, and present results to the team
  • Drive manufacturing and supplier activities including part preparation, first-article inspection, and validation
  • Build and improve engineering and documentation processes that outlast your co-op term
  • Partner with senior engineers and program leaders, and present progress in design and program reviews

What We Are Looking For

  • Enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, with the ability to commit to a minimum 6-month co-op rotation
  • Available for a full-time term, whether a full academic semester, summer plus a connecting semester, or two consecutive semesters
  • Strong curiosity and willingness to work across disciplines
  • Comfortable in a lab or shop environment with hardware and tools
  • Clear communicator who can document work, present results, and ask thoughtful questions
  • Prior hands-on experience through projects, labs, clubs, personal builds, or a previous internship or co-op is a strong plus

What You Will Gain

OUR CLUB

Seattle Sounders FC is a progressive high performing collection of people who strive to achieve the highest levels of our sport while making a transformative impact in our communities in the best soccer city in America. Our culture is focused on serving one of the most passionate sports fan bases in North America who are invested in the Sounders as much for our commitment to making a positive impact in our communities as they are for winning the 2019 MLS Cup, 2022 CONCACAF Champions League and 2025 Leagues Cup on home soil. We exist to create special moments like these, where we enrich lives and unify our fans and city through soccer.

 

POSITION SUMMARY 

Seattle Sounders FC Performance team is offering an educational internship during Spring, Summer and/or Fall immersion blocks in 2027.  This internship offers unique experiences to strengthen learning and engage skillsets within Performance Training. Students will gain invaluable experience in a professional sports setting and an understanding of program design.

Eligible candidates must have at a minimum a Bachelor’s degree and certification from NSCA-CSCS, CSCCa, and/or USAW. Ideally students are able to commit for approximately 650 hours and start and end dates will be determined with each intern.

 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES 

  • Support and Collaboration: Play a crucial role in supporting the performance, science, and nutrition sectors within the Seattle Sounders FC, aiding all teams within the club.
  • Training Assistance: Assist in the setup and execution of all First and Second team training sessions, including GPS tracking, warm-up routines, and on-field conditioning.
  • Session Preparation: Help prepare and conduct First and Second team mobility, lifting, and activation sessions.
  • Data Analysis: Support the collection and analysis of GPS, monitoring, and performance testing data.
  • Work Environment: Contribute to a dynamic, ambitious, and enjoyable work atmosphere.
  • Assist with the setup and breakdown of weight room and field equipment.
  • Maintain cleanliness and order of the weight room and its equipment.
  • Support during lifting and field sessions through supervision and demonstration.
  • Participate in Performance Science Innovation and Initiatives.
  • Contribute to the design, development, and delivery of curriculum projects as determined by the Performance Staff.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree and certification from NSCA-CSCS, CSCCa, and/or USAW.
  • CPR/AED certification is mandatory.
  • This is an unpaid internship. Must be able to receive academic credit towards a credited program.
  • Affiliation agreement must be executed between University and Seattle Sounders prior to start.
  • Exceptional communication skills to deliver programs effectively and interact professionally with colleagues, players, and coaches.
  • A keen interest in soccer or sports in general.
  • An enthusiastic and proactive approach to tasks.
  • Excellent organization abilities, with a knack for managing workloads, prioritizing tasks, and adhering to deadlines efficiently.
  • Must have a keen eye and attention for detail.
  • Proficiency in computer use and quick to learn new software and processes.

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

  • This position will work from Sounders FC Headquarters & Training Facility in Renton WA and attending meetings and matches as needed.
  • Must be able to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.
  • Must be able to facilitate own local travel.
  • Must reside within Washington state upon date of hire.
  • Must be eligible to work in the US without sponsorship.
  • Must adhere to the MLS Next Safety and Well-Being policy and any other relevant child safety policies.

Shift delivers AI agents that transform insurers' most critical work. By combining deep industry expertise and unmatched data resources, Shift provides proven results that have earned the trust of hundreds of the world's leading insurers. Our culture is built on innovation, trust, and a drive to transform the insurance industry through our SaaS platform. We come from more than 50 different countries and cultures and together we are creating the future of insurance.

Learn more at www.shift-technology.com

 

Shift Technology : 

Shift is the leading AI platform for insurance. Shift combines generative, agentic, and predictive AI to detect fraud, assess risk, and recommend actions throughout the claims process. Our teams tackle complex data challenges and bring advanced models into production at scale, giving insurers deeper insights into their data while helping their customers get paid faster and enjoy a smoother claims experience. Our technology is adopted and trusted by the world’s leading insurers.

The QA Engineering Team 🧪:

The Quality Assurance team, part of Engineering, makes sure that Shift can ship fast and safely. Our AI-driven software is deployed for insurers worldwide, across many multi-tenant environments, and we use Generative AI, LLM agents, and modern automation to solve quality challenges at this scale. Here are just a few of the areas we work on:

  • Release validation: risk-based testing and delivery automation;
  • Automated regression suites and test automation;
  • Functional test coverage and test gap analysis;
  • Test data generation and test environment provisioning;
  • AI-powered QA tooling, built with LLMs and agents, that engineers and QA leads use every day

title: Software Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)

description:
About the Role

At Sigma, we’re not just adding AI—we’re building the future of how people work with data. Our platform already lets users explore billions of rows of data in seconds with a spreadsheet-like interface, analyze and present their data in workbooks, and build data apps and workflows. Now we’re pushing further, applying AI to reshape how people build in Sigma, discover insights, and make smarter decisions—fast. You can learn more about our vision for AI/ML at Sigma in our blog post.

That’s where you come in. As an AI/ML PhD Intern, you’ll join a growing team focused on building the AI foundation that will power Sigma for the future. Your work will become an integral part of the workflow for the thousands of enterprises that run on Sigma. We're looking for PhD students that are passionate about the intersection of AI, business, and data. 

What You’ll Do

  • Conduct original AI/ML research in search, recommendations, natural language processing, agentic workflows and more
  • Prototype and productionize AI systems that feel intuitive but do a lot under the hood
  • Tackle novel UX problems at the intersection of AI, analytics, and data apps
  • Contribute to the development of scalable AI/ML infrastructure for experimentation, training, and evaluation of large-scale models.

What You Bring

  • Current PhD student studying AI/ML at a U.S. accredited university
  • Deep understanding of machine learning, including deep learning algorithms, model architectures and optimization
  • Baseline understanding of building and deploying production-grade AI/ML systems
  • Knowledge of the full ML lifecycle: data curation, training, deployment, monitoring
  • Desire to bridge research and application—bringing new AI ideas from concept to impactful deployment.

Bonus Points (or skills you’ll build here)

  • You've built agents that can plan, reason, and use tools
  • You’ve fine-tuned or trained foundation models (language or multimodal) for novel domains
  • You know your way around cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure)
  • You’ve worked in a fast-moving startup or high-growth environment

Additional Job details

The hourly rate range for this position is $80-$90 an hour

Compensation may vary outside of this range depending on a number of factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies and experience. Base pay is one part of the Total Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work at Sigma Computing.

Our advanced technology, combined with a team genuinely invested in our clients’ success, creates frictionless shopping experiences, approving more good orders, protecting revenue, and keeping customers happy.

Trusted by thousands of leading merchants across more than 100 countries, we securely process billions of transactions each year. Our people are the heart of everything we do, driving our mission forward with commitment, empathy, and creativity. Join us on our mission to empower confident, fraud-free commerce by helping online retailers provide superior customer experiences and eliminate fraud. Learn about our company values here!

Signifyd is one of the world’s leading tech start-ups! They develop best-in-class AI fraud prevention software; which helps make the world a better place. As an intern, you'll be given a masterclass into the software development lifecycle. You'll get to work with amazing colleagues on complex challenges. Within your first week as an intern, you'll be deploying code changes that affect millions of online orders. It's an exceptional place to work, with an awesome culture & work-life balance.

As an Engineering Intern, you’ll make things happen!

Our Intern Software Engineers will have the opportunity to gain industry-leading insight, guidance and support to learn our technology stack and grow very quickly into fully productive members of our team; no bench sitting!  

If you want help, you'll get it - from all quarters - but we’ll encourage you to figure out what needs to be done, identify who is in the best position to make it happen; and if that’s you, roll up your sleeves and get stuck in! 

Our Signifyd stack: Java, Cassandra, ElasticSearch, BigQuery, MySQL, Apache Spark, Play! framework, gRPC, Linux, Docker, Kubernetes, GCP, AI (Claude, Cursor) 

What support can you expect:

We’ll provide you with a solid investment in your individual growth and development including an individual development plan, mentoring from industry professionals, and a spot on a small peer-led team to provide great opportunities to learn.

What you’ll get to do:

  • From the outset you’ll contribute to our features and products and participate fully in your team’s responsibilities

  • Be part of a team who are responsible for the full lifecycle of their products: design, development, unit testing, integration testing, deployment, monitoring and iterative improvement
  • Be part of a team who are responsible for the full technology stack related to their product or feature; from the user level APIs right down to the databases, streams, and queues, that back the functionality

To know if we’re a great fit for you, you’ll:

  • Be working towards a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or Software Engineering 
  • Have an interest or desire to work with Java, Python, SQL or any of our development stack, or you’ll have worked with some of our stack before on your own time or for your own projects
  • Be willing to ask for help if you need it
  • Be comfortable making a mistake, but be willing to learn from it
  • Be open to learning from others and always curious to know more

What will you get in return:

  • A competitive base salary
  • 16 days of annual leave plus 8 public holidays
  • Free snacks and drinks in the office
  • Have a great setup and working environment to help you do your job

description:
About the Company:

At SK hynix memory solutions, we're at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, developing advanced memory solutions that power everything from smartphones to data centers. As a global leader in NAND flash technology and memory solutions, we drive the evolution of advancing mobile technology, empowering cloud computing, and pioneering future technologies. Our cutting-edge memory technologies are essential in today's most advanced electronic devices and IT infrastructure, enabling enhanced performance and user experiences across the digital landscape.

We're looking for innovative minds to join our mission of shaping the future of technology. At SK hynix memory solutions, you'll be part of a team that's pioneering breakthrough memory solutions while maintaining a strong commitment to sustainability. We're not just adapting to technological change – we're driving it, with significant investments in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and eco-friendly solutions and operational practices. As we continue to expand our market presence and push the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor technology, we invite you to be part of our journey to creating the next generation of memory solutions that will define the future of computing.

 

Internship Duration: 6 months

Hours: 40 hours per week

Start Date: Immediately (September/October 2026) 

Location: San Jose

 

About the role:

We are hiring a research intern in loop engineering: best practices for closed-loop flows that automate, optimize, and explore SoC designs. These are AI-assisted hardware/software co-design flows. CHIA, from UC Berkeley, is one example of a framework you may use.

You will own a scoped research question with a full-time researcher: build or extend the loop, run the experiments, and write up what the results mean for design automation.

 

What you will do:

  • Study how a design loop should be structured: which steps belong in it, what feedback each step returns, and how search, verification, and physical-design results drive the next iteration.
  • Implement the loop with languages and tools such as Chisel and XLS, together with simulation, software build, and physical-design tools.
  • Apply it to an SoC problem such as microarchitectural exploration, RTL implementation and verification, or power, performance, and area optimization.
  • Compare loop designs on the quality of the design point, the cost of the search, reproducibility, reuse, and how reliably a failure is diagnosed.
  • Make the loop reliable enough to rerun: clear interfaces between steps, cached results, regression checks, and reports that support a conclusion.

 

What you bring:

  • Progress toward a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.
  • Coursework or project experience in loop engineering, computer architecture, digital design, VLSI, or electronic design automation.
  • Fluency in Python, and comfort reading and changing an existing codebase.
  • Ability to pose a small research question, keep a record of what changed, and explain the result.

 

Preferred:

  • Exposure to RTL (Verilog, SystemVerilog, Chisel, or XLS) or to an SoC design framework.
  • Experience with an architecture simulator or with RTL simulation.
  • Familiarity with an AI-assisted hardware/software co-design loop framework, such as CHIA, or with scripted hardware design, verification, or design-space exploration flows.

 

What success looks like:

By the end of your internship, you will have a rerunnable co-design loop applied to an SoC problem, a comparison of what worked and what it cost, and a short report on the practice the team should adopt.

 

COMPENSATION: $35/hr - $45/hr

description:

We inform and empower decision makers, policy professionals and citizens through our award-winning journalism and data – delivering profound insights to help our customers decode and act on state politics and  policy. We’re building a category-defining business that will reshape America as we strengthen visibility into what’s happening and why at the state level.

As a Software Engineering Intern, you’ll join our engineering team in Washington, DC and ship real features to real users, not side projects. You’ll work across the full stack: React/Next.js interfaces, Node APIs, and Postgres data models that keep up with petabyte-scale content. One sprint you might help prototype a semantic-search UI backed by vector embeddings. The next, you might build part of a real-time collaboration layer that lets policy analysts co-author annotations and compare version histories without refreshing the page.

As a Software Engineering Intern, you will:

  • Ship vertical product slices with your mentor and team: Figma wireframe, React component, Node handler, SQL/Mongo query, deployed on AWS via Docker and GitHub Actions.
  • Help build fast, delightful data workflows such as instant search, real-time diffing and collaborative annotation, with sub-200 ms interactions over large datasets.

description:
Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

Overview: Before a single transistor gets placed, someone has to decide what the chip should actually be and ensure it functions to specs. This team makes those calls including System on a Chip (SoC) -level architecture, fabric/interconnect design, verification and not just core compute.

What you might work on: This posting spans multiple teams within Hardware Architecture & AI Hardware and SoC . One application, one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team and location that fits best. What each team does: 

  • Architecture: We define and evaluate the system, CPU, memory, fabric, and chiplet-level decisions that shape future products. We analyze workloads, performance, power, and system requirements, develop architectural models, do tradeoff analyses, and specifications for implementation.
  • AI Hardware: We design and develop the core AI accelerator IP, including compute, data movement, and other specialized hardware blocks that enable high-performance AI workloads. We take these IPs from requirements through RTL design, verification, and delivery for SoC integration.
  • SOC : Our team is where everything comes together. We design and verify the integration of all subsystems and the final pieces that allow the chip to interact with the outside world; scaleout, memory and on-chip system management and security. We validate cross functional and performance requirements, and ultimately take the design to silicon. 

 

Who You Are

  • Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, ECE, CE, or CS.
  • Coursework or projects in digital design, computer architecture and performance modeling.
  • Self-starter who brings sound judgment and practical problem-solving to every project with a solid interest in AI and hardware, along with the ability to take ownership and deliver results.

 

What We Need

  • Familiarity with ASIC design concepts, ranging from performance simulations, RTL design / verification,  and logic synthesis / timing analysis 
  • Scripting & programming skills (example: Python, PERL, tcl, C/C++); with experience using AI coding platforms
  • [Architecture] Experience with architectural simulators.
  • Exposure to RISC-V or other open ISAs is nice to have.
  • FPGA design experience is nice to have.

 

What You Will Learn

  • Taking designs from specification to RTL to verification, and learning the qualification checks and tools needed to do so.
  • How architectural tradeoffs (Architecture: Compute vs. memory vs. interconnect.  AI HW/ SOC: Power, Performance & Area) get decided with data, not intuition.
  • Best practices for cross-functional collaboration, seeing firsthand how Architecture, RTL, Software, and Physical Design teams stay aligned through implementation.
  • Practical methods to integrate AI tools directly into your daily technical workflow.
  • [Architecture] Performance modeling methodology used before RTL existed.

  • System Software: Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware.
  • System Design: The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint.
  • System Architecture: Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals.

Who You Are

  • Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog).
  • Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical.
  • Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs).

description: Field AI is transforming how robots interact with the real world. We are building risk-aware, reliable, and field-ready AI systems that address the most complex challenges in robotics, unlocking the full potential of embodied intelligence. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-based architectures, and are charting a new course, with already-globally-deployed solutions delivering real-world results and rapidly improving models through real-field applications. Hardware Team: The Hardware Team at Field AI develops perception and compute payloads that power autonomous robotics systems in complex real world environments. Our work spans the full hardware stack designing and integrating sensing systems (LiDAR, camera, TOF, IMU, GPS), embedded compute (CPUs, GPUs, microcontrollers, Linux, ROS), electrical systems (power distribution, communication), and mechanical components (structures, thermal regulation, ingress protection). The team focuses on both development (research, design, prototyping, testing) and operations (production, testing, QA, debugging). We’re a small, fast-moving team, and we care deeply about improving: 1) core capabilities, 2) system reliability, 3) system scalability. As a growing team we are also building operational systems and procedures from the ground up. Mechanical Systems Role: As a Mechanical Engineer Intern on the Hardware Team at Field AI, you will contribute to the design and implementation of mechanical systems that house and support sensing and compute platforms in real-world environments. From ruggedized enclosures to thermal management to manufacturability, your work will be critical to ensuring our systems operate reliably in the field. Responsibilities may span the full lifecycle from CAD through production to field support. You will collaborate closely with electrical, compute, and systems engineers to build tightly integrated solutions ready for deployment in challenging field environments. Additionally while your focus will be on mechanical systems you will likely contribute across all hardware domains. What You Will Get To Do Mechanical System Design Structures: Design and model mechanical structures including external enclosures, internal compute frames, and load-bearing chassis. Mounts: Design and validate robust sensor mounts, payload attachment points, and mechanical interfaces. Ingress Protection: Implement IP-rated solutions with gaskets, seals, membranes, and coatings to meet water/dust ingress standards. Thermal Management: Incorporate thermal mitigation strategies such as fans, heat sinks, conductive paths, and airflow guides. Mass & Volume Budgets: Ensure adherence to payload constraints, including tight volumetric envelopes and weight limitations. Mechanical System Implementation CAD & Simulation: Build detailed SolidWorks CAD assemblies. Run FEA and thermal simulations to validate strength, durability, and heat dissipation. Material & Component Selection: Choose materials and components to meet mass, strength, thermal, and manufacturability constraints. Design for Production: Apply DFM, DFA, DFS principles throughout the design lifecycle. System Testing: Conduct mechanical load testing (shock, vibration), thermal validation, ingress tests, and sensor alignment assessments. Prototyping: Rapidly iterate on prototypes for fit checks, thermal evaluations, and integration trials. Documentation & Budgets: Generate mechanical drawings, GD&T annotations, BOMs, and assembly instructions for fabrication and QA. Manage weight, volume, and thermal budgets. Mechanical System Production & Servicing Build: Work with vendors and contract manufacturers to procure mechanical hardware. Develop QA checks for incoming units. Support payload integration and scaling. Debug: Investigate mechanical failures, deformation, and environmental weaknesses during testing and deployments. Monitor: Develop protocols for monitoring the system mechanical health and loads. What You Have Education: Current student pursuing a B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or related field. CAD Expertise: Proficient with SolidWorks or equivalent mechanical CAD platforms. Thermal & Structural Analysis: Familiarity with FEA and thermal modeling tools. description: GenBio AI is an AI for Science company on a mission to make biology fully computable. Our first step toward that mission is AIDO Cell , the first virtual cell world model that holistically simulates cell biology from molecules up to whole-cell behavior. description: The Koch Internship Program (KIP) is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Eligible candidates will be geographically located in and authorized to work in the United States through the duration of the program. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the admissions process early! Overview The Fulcrum Foundation seeks an intern to support its state regulatory and permitting reform work. The intern will work directly with the Policy Director and Legal Director as well as other members of the management team, and the intern's work product will feed into briefings, model legislation, and other materials used by state legislators, governors' offices, and executive agencies. Responsibilities Research state statutes, regulations, and guidance documents to identify and analyze state regulatory reform initiatives and potential. Verify legal citations in Foundation written materials for accuracy and completeness. Test AI tools to assess how well they handle different kinds of regulatory analysis. Build simple AI-powered applications to support research on regulatory questions. Review draft materials and provide suggested edits for accuracy, readability, and persuasiveness. Write and publish short written pieces, including blog posts or brief op eds, on regulatory reform issues (as opportunities arise). Qualifications Current law or public policy student or recent graduate, or prior experience working with statutes, regulations, and other legal materials. Strong attention to detail and comfort experimenting with new software tools. No programming background required; experience with AI tools or low-code platforms is a plus. Familiarity with cost-benefit analysis is helpful but not required.

description: The Koch Internship Program (KIP) is a paid experiential learning program run by Stand Together Fellowships that offers professional development, leadership training, and meaningful work experience at non-profits tackling some of our nation's most pressing policy challenges all over the United States. Overview The Fulcrum Foundation seeks an intern to support research on state government regulatory policy and its effects on economic growth, entrepreneurship, labor markets, housing, occupational licensing, permitting, and related public policy issues. Interns will work closely with senior researchers to gather and organize data, review proposed rules and administrative records, assist with research for public comment letters submitted to state agencies and legislatures, and contribute to policy briefs and reports intended for policymakers and the broader public. The internship is designed for undergraduate students, recent graduates, and early-stage graduate or law students interested in public policy, economics, law, or government. Prior research experience is helpful but not required; we are looking for careful, curious people who write well and can work independently in a remote setting. Research Areas Potential areas of work include: Administrative law, rulemaking, and the public comment process Occupational licensing Business permitting and approvals Housing and land-use regulation Small business and entrepreneurship policy State economic development Regulatory impact analysis Government modernization and process reform Labor market regulation Institutional determinants of economic growth Responsibilities Assist with research for public comment letters on proposed state rules and regulations, including reviewing rulemaking notices, summarizing proposed rule text and agency justifications, and identifying relevant statutes, prior comments, and existing research. Help draft and fact-check sections of comment letters, and compile supporting evidence, citations, and data appendices under the direction of senior staff. Track state regulatory proposals, legislative activity, and agency actions relevant to Fulcrum’s research agenda. Collect, organize, and document data from government websites, administrative records, and other publicly available sources. Help maintain measures of regulatory burden, permitting processes, occupational licensing requirements, and related policy variables. Conduct literature reviews and summarize academic and policy research for ongoing projects. Draft sections of policy briefs, research summaries, and other written products, and assist with editing and citation. Assist with basic descriptive analysis, tables, and charts using spreadsheet or statistical software. Participate in research team meetings and contribute to project planning. Qualifications Required: Current undergraduate, graduate, or law student, or recent graduate, in economics, public policy, political science, law, public administration, or a related field. Strong writing skills and attention to detail. Ability to read and accurately summarize dense material such as proposed rules, statutes, and academic research. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets. Ability to work independently and meet deadlines in a remote environment. Located in and authorized to work in the United States for the duration of the program, and able to attend all required KIP programming, including the two-day summit in Arlington, Virginia. Preferred: Coursework in economics, statistics, public policy, or administrative law. Familiarity with R, Stata, Python, or another statistical program (not required). Prior research experience through coursework, a research assistant position, or an internship. Interest in state government policy, regulatory institutions, and economic development.
